EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The best Sharpe from 400 backtested configurations should not be reported as expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the maximum from many backtests creates selection bias and does not give an unbiased live-performance estimate.

items.says: The futures-signal result appears to be claimed again in the Kaggle project.
items.because: Both entries describe an order-book imbalance signal improving a futures book over 18 months out of sample.

items.says: The futures-signal result appears to duplicate the Northpeak claim.
items.because: Both entries describe an order-book imbalance signal improving a futures book over 18 months out of sample.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker may undermine the Monte Carlo study.
items.because: Workers can generate duplicate or correlated random streams rather than independent simulations.

items.says: Define the risk-adjusted-return metric and its comparison baseline.
items.because: The 35% improvement is difficult to interpret without them.

items.says: Distinguish the 35% improvement from the later Sharpe result.
items.because: They may describe related or overlapping results.

items.says: Identify the baseline for the Sharpe change and its relationship to the 35% improvement.
items.because: The two performance claims may overlap.

items.says: Make sure the code portfolio link is clickable, relevant and current.
Consider adding a research area or dissertation topic.
items.because: It could support the roles being targeted.

items.says: Consider whether present-tense wording would better distinguish the current bakery role.
items.because: The current past-tense verbs do not distinguish ongoing responsibilities from completed results.

items.says: Clarify whether the six people were direct reports or the team working the shifts.
Specify the result or scope of staying within the weekly labour budget if it can be substantiated.
Use the U.S. spelling “labor” for a U.S.-based résumé.
Clarify the measurement period and scale of the reduction from 12% to 7%.
items.because: The result should be unmistakably stated as percentages of production or percentage-point values.

items.says: Qualify the claim that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: The split design alone may not establish that feature construction, model selection and all tuning met that standard.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the feature store.
Explain what reuse by the research team meant.
items.because: The feature count alone does not show the store’s impact.

items.says: Distinguish approval for a future allocation from an allocation that actually went live.
items.because: A live outcome should be stated only if it can be substantiated.

items.says: If retaining the parameter-selection work, report a properly held-out estimate.
items.because: The best backtested Sharpe is not a defensible live expectation.

items.says: Clarify whether the 18-month period was held out from all model and parameter selection.
Consider moving the Sharpe result ahead of the methodological bullets.
items.because: The outcome would be easier to find.

items.says: Replace the redundant phrase “running the runs.”
Include the hardware or computing setup if helpful.
items.because: It could make the runtime comparison more meaningful.

items.says: Clarify mathematically what tightening the bound by a log factor means.
Keep the manuscript status precise rather than making the result sound accepted or published.
items.because: The paper is under review.

items.says: Identify your authorship role if appropriate.
Add the response count or evaluation context for the 4.8/5 rating if available.
items.because: The rating can be hard to assess without that context.

items.says: Include an accessible repository or package link.

items.because: The count should reflect meaningful downloads rather than an automated or cumulative statistic.

items.because: Readers cannot tell how the project performed.
